title: Classify Once, Project Many
claim: A semantic primitive should be classified once into canonical objects and typed edges; proof, dependency, blast-radius, dispute, evolution, topology, Reality-Mirror, and related maps should be derived as deterministic projections whenever their membership can be computed from those canonical primitives.
assumptions: Typed edges preserve their native semantics.
A view definition can select/filter canonical objects and edges without changing their identity.
definitions: Semantic primitive: a meaning-bearing classification that cannot be deterministically inferred from already admitted structure.
Projection: a deterministic selection, aggregation, layout, statistic, or derived membership over canonical objects and typed edges.
negative_guards: Do not call the API again to decide map membership when existing canonical edges already determine it.
Do not create duplicate edges merely to satisfy multiple visualizations.
Do not let a projection silently mutate the canonical source object.
kill_conditions: A target map repeatedly requires semantic information not represented by any canonical object/edge and not derivable by deterministic rules.

ledger.meaning: Registered classify-once/store-once/project-many as the anti-duplication rule for Atlas views.
ledger.limits: If a future view genuinely requires a new semantic primitive, the grammar must record that explicitly rather than pretending it is deterministic.
